title: A unique μ8-silicate-bridged octametallic [Dy8SiO4] complex exhibiting slow magnetic relaxation

synthesis.procedure: H2L was prepared by condensation of anthranilic acid (0.342 g, 2.5 mmol) and o-vanillin (0.384 g, 2.5 mmol) in 100 mL ethanol by a previously reported method. Complex 1 was obtained from a mixture of Dy(NO3)3·6H2O (0.1 mmol, 45 mg), Na2SiO3 (0.05 mmol, 6 mg), NaOH (0.25 mmol, 10 mg), H2L (0.25 mmol, 68 mg) and 10 mL ethanol, heated at 75 °C for 2 days, which afforded yellow crystals. Yield 35% based on the metal salt. The anthranilate ligands in the product arise from decomposition of H2L.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: heating in ethanol; vessel not specified
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Yellow crystals of 1 isolated after heating.

properties.summary: Field-induced slow magnetic relaxation is reported. Static data from 2–300 K at 1000 Oe give χmT = 109.73 emu mol−1 K at 300 K (slightly below 113.36 emu mol−1 K for eight free Dy(III) ions), a Curie–Weiss fit over 5.5–300 K, and a low-temperature drop to 81.07 emu mol−1 K attributed to anisotropy and/or weak antiferromagnetic coupling. Magnetization reaches 43.16 μB at 1.8 K and 7 T, below the isotropic saturation value, and M vs H/T curves do not superimpose. AC susceptibility (10–997 Hz) shows frequency-dependent in- and out-of-phase signals below 12 K without a maximum above 2 K; a kink near 8 K at 997 Hz becomes clearer under a 600 Oe dc field used to suppress QTM, but no peak maximum is observed and no relaxation barrier is extracted.
